Fig. 1. Current challenges in mixed autonomy and the path toward better human-machine interaction. Mixed autonomy poses challenges 
in aligning AV behavior with human drivers. Our evaluation and data attribution framework guides the development of interpretable, human-like 
LLM agents for smoother traﬃc integration.

Fig. 2. Introduction to the human-likeness evaluation framework. This framework evaluates human-likeness from both short-term and long-
term perspectives, capturing performance variations across diverse driving scenarios and over extended periods. Through the application of data 
attribution, it also reveals the information reliance patterns of humans and machines, providing insights to optimize information ﬂow and enhance 
human-machine collaboration.

Fig. 3. Overview of proposed HermesSense dataset, benchmark and workﬂow. HermesSense integrates real-world multimodal driving data, 
including visual, textual, numerical, and human inputs to generate prompts for LLM-based driving agents. The benchmark evaluates human-likeness 
through short-term decision alignment, statistical similarity across driver types, and a feature attribution framework for selecting optimal information 
ﬂow in driving agents.
Fig. 4. Annotation platform illustrating the driving scene clips and vehicle-dynamics traces used for driving behavior labeling.
Fig. 5. A prompt example for #846 instance.

Fig. 6. LLMs’ decision alignment across various scenarios. We evaluate model performance on speed control, turning, and steering decisions using F1 
score and 𝔻ali across varying conditions, including time of day, location type, and intersection presence. Higher F1 scores indicate better behavioral 
alignment, while lower 𝔻ali reﬂect greater distributional similarity.

Fig. 7. Statistical analysis of driving behavior across diﬀerent groups. (a) By driving style: aggressive, moderate, and defensive. (b) By gender: 
female vs. male drivers. (c) By driving experience: less vs. more experienced drivers. (d) By driver age: younger vs. older drivers. Each subﬁgure 
summarizes the average and variability of brake input, throttle input, and speed.

Fig. 8. Results of the human-likeness of LLMs across various driver types. Overall statistical human-likeness of all LLM agents across diﬀerent driver 
proﬁles. Each circle represents an individual LLM agent’s human-likeness score.
